REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - APRIL 27, 2017 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT HELD ON APRIL 27,
2017, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Father Tony Gomez, St. Linus Catholic Church,
  Norwalk, CA.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was given by the Rookie I/II Division “Angels.”

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in
  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations presented to:

  STACKED Restaurant (Business Spotlight)

  Valley Christian High School Crusaders Soccer Team (California Interscholastic
  Federation Southern Section Division 6 Champions)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Mel Cortez expressed concerns regarding the expenditures for the Cerritos Astor
  Museum, the budget, the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts, the Calmet
  contract, and the sale of the property on Studebaker.

  Murali Vasudevan congratulated the newly elected Councilmembers and expressed
  concerns with the low membership of the ABCUSD PTA and bullet voting.

  Tom Tislow congratulated the newly elected Councilmembers and expressed support
  for the Sheriff’s Department who responded to a burglary in his neighborhood. He
  thanked the City for their support of the adaptive recreation programs.

  Gavin Riley thanked all members of the City Council. He expressed concerns with the
  infrastructure of the City and suggested the City Council revisit a sales tax measure.

  Sam Desai congratulated the newly elected Councilmembers, requested that
  PowerPoint Presentations be posted along with the agenda, and expressed concerns
  with the CalMet contract and the status of the Studebaker property.

  Murali Vasudevan requested minutes transcription services.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of April
  13, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of April 13, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu

  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated April 27, 2017
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated April 27, 2017 in the amount

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL APPROVING AND CERTIFYING THE NEGATIVE

  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 2017-2, AND PRECISE PLAN 2017-4 FOR A

  (APN 7038-014-019) (COUNCIL).*

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE
  OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AMENDING SECTION 22.40.950 OF THE
  CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO DRIVE-THROUGH SERVICE

  CERRITOS, HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2017-3

  THROUGH SERVICE ATM AT 18801 GRIDLEY ROAD, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA,
  90703. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS ZONED REGIONAL COMMERCIAL (CR) (APN
  7038-014-019) (COUNCIL).*

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Levi Javier inquired as to any potential toxic waste that may be left behind at the
  Allen Tire Co. building.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments and the public hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to:

  1. Approve the Negative Declaration for Development Code Amendment 2017-3,

  CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO DRIVE-THROUGH SERVICE

  CODE AMENDMENT 2017-3; and

  PROPERTY OWNER MACERICH CERRITOS ADJACENT, LLC, TO PERMIT
  A BANK USE WITH A DETACHED DRIVE-THROUGH SERVICE ATM AT
  18801 GRIDLEY ROAD, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT

  019); and

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for Del Amo Boulevard
  rehabilitation between Bloomfield Avenue and Norwalk Boulevard, Project No.
  14713, Bid No. 1298-17 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $1,146,530 for Del Amo Boulevard
  Rehabilitation – Bloomfield Avenue to Norwalk Boulevard, Project No. 14713,
  Bid No. 1298-17, to Sequel Contractors and reject all other bids; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for Bid No. 1297-17, Cerritos
  Center for the Performing Arts Sierra Room roof replacement, Project No. 12706

  A staff report was Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to

  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to authorize the
  City Manager to execute the subrecipient agreement with the Los Angeles Gateway

  associated agreement amendment (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9E.  Review of the Combined Financial Program for the City of Cerritos and the City of
  Cerritos as Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency for Fiscal Year 2017-
  2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  A staff report was given by Art Gallucci, City Manager, and Ryan Carey, Budget
  Manager. A PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Anantha Ramachandran expressed concerns that a large portion of the projected
  surplus will go to support the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts and the Cerritos
  Astor Museum and would rather the funds be spend on tree trimming, road
  maintenance, and sidewalk repair.

  Murali Vasudevan requested that the PowerPoint Presentations be posted along with
  the agenda and expressed concerns about the expenditures related to the operation
  of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.

  Sam Desai offered his experience in finance and budgeting and offered classes to the
  City Council in order for them to better understand the City’s budget document.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: By unanimous City Council concurrence, this item was continued to the
  meeting of May 17, 2017 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:
